claim: The classic Lavaux Route 113 from St-Saphorin to Lutry is 11.6 km, takes about 4 hours, with 200 m of ascent and 500 m of descent.
quote: Distance: 11.6 km ... Duration: Approximately 4 hours ... Elevation Gain: 200m up, 500m down ... The trail follows 'Route 113 – Terrasses de Lavaux' through wine terraces along Lake Geneva's north shore.

claim: Shorter Lavaux options include St-Saphorin to Cully (6.5 km, ~2 h) and the downhill Chexbres to St-Saphorin (~3 km).
quote: Half-Distance Route: St Saphorin to Cully - Distance: 6.5 km - Duration: ~2 hours ... Minimal Route: Chexbres to St Saphorin - Distance: ~3 km - Direction: Downhill only

claim: AllTrails lists the St-Saphorin to Lutry vineyard terraces hike at about 7 miles (~11 km), 3.5-4 hours.
quote: The Lavaux Vineyard Terraces trail from St-Saphorin to Lutry covers 7 miles (approximately 11 km) and takes about 3.5–4 hours to complete.

claim: The full long-distance 'Discovering the Terraces of Lavaux' trail is about 35 km and ~8h30; Rivaz, St-Saphorin and Chexbres each have their own rail stations.
quote: The full 'Discovering the Terraces of Lavaux' long-distance trail (GT) spans '35 km' and 'should take around 8h30' ... All three towns (Rivaz, St Saphorin, Chexbres) 'have railway stations'

claim: Lavaux Vinorama in Rivaz showcases roughly 300 wines (notably Chasselas and indigenous Plant Robert) from across the eight Lavaux appellations.
quote: about 300 wines from across all the Lavaux vineyards including many Chasselas, the region's iconic grape variety, as well as elegant and powerful reds, white specialities and sweet wines

claim: Vinorama screens an 8-language documentary following a year in the life of a Lavaux winegrowing family and is open Mon-Sat 10:30-20:00, Sun until 19:00.
quote: An ultra-modern screening room features a documentary available in eight languages that follows 'the year of a Lavaux vine-growing family' ... Hours: Monday–Saturday 10:30–20:00; Sunday 10:30–19:00

claim: The Lavaux Express tourist train runs two main 1h15 loops at CHF 17 from April 1 to November 1 2026: Lutry-Aran-Grandvaux-Lutry and Cully-Riex-Epesses-Dezaley-Cully.
quote: Lutry Loop (CHF 17.-) ... Villages visited: 'Lutry - Aran - Grandvaux - Lutry' - Duration: 1 hour 15 minutes ... Cully Loop (CHF 17.-) ... 'Cully - Riex - Epesses - Dézaley - Cully' - Duration: 1 hour 15 minutes ... Operating: April 1 – November 1, 2026

claim: Themed Lavaux Express rides include a Caveau Train with 3-wine tasting + souvenir glass (CHF 28, Fri-Sun 18:30) and a Cully Aperitif Train (CHF 25, Thursdays).
quote: Caveau Train (CHF 28.-) ... Features: 'Taste 3 wines + a souvenir glass' ... Aperitif Train (CHF 25.-) - Departure point: Cully pier - Duration: 1 hour 30 minutes with '45 minute stop-aperitif in the vineyards of Aran'

claim: CGN boats from Lausanne-Ouchy reach Lutry in ~18 min, Cully in ~33 min and Rivaz-St-Saphorin in ~47 min, with 2-5 daily round trips mid-April to late October.
quote: Lausanne-Ouchy: 0:00 (departure) - Lutry: 0:18 - Cully: 0:33 - Rivaz-St Saphorin: 0:47 ... Peak Season (mid-April to late October): 'two round-trip cruises...are possible daily from Lausanne and a further three from Vevey'

claim: SBB regional trains link Lausanne to Cully in roughly 8-10 minutes, running about every 15 minutes, with stops in Pully, Lutry, Villette, Cully, Epesses, Rivaz and St-Saphorin.
quote: The fastest way to get from Lausanne to Cully is by train which takes 10 minutes ... Swiss Federal Railways (SBB CFF FFS) operates a train from Lausanne to Cully every 15 minutes ... The R4 ... stops at Pully, Lutry, Villette, Cully, Epesses, Rivaz, and St Saphorin between Lausanne and Vevey

claim: Saint-Saphorin is a celebrated Lavaux appellation between Epesses and Chardonne whose vineyards are planted overwhelmingly with Chasselas.
quote: Saint-Saphorin village lies on the steep northern shores of Lake Geneva, in Lavaux, Switzerland. Located immediately west of Chardonne and east of Puidoux and Epesses ... A typical vineyard in Saint-Saphorin is planted mostly with Fendant, or Chasselas

claim: Cully's 16th-19th-century winegrowers' houses make it a natural base for Lavaux, while Epesses is a tiny hamlet perched above the lake.
quote: Cully is an excellent starting point for exploring the vineyard terraces, with its historic center featuring narrow streets and picturesque winegrowers' houses dating from the 16th to 19th century. Tiny Epesses is nestled on a hillside above Lake Geneva
